transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-09 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Nora (Firetrail Head of Platform), Evan (CTO), Priya (Infra), Samir (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Firetrail is evaluating Redwood for GPU-backed inference across cloud and private options. Key drivers: predictable unit cost, VPC/on-prem connectivity, SOC2 & ISO compliance, and a short pilot to validate latency and throughput. They expressed interest in Dedicated/reserved capacity but want a clear fall-back to hosted and an on-prem option for regulated customers. Action: send security docs, pricing, and schedule benchmark.

Topics covered:
- Current infra and cloud providers (GCP + colo)
- Data residency and compliance needs (EU customers)
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs and autoscaling/bursting
- Network peering / VPC options for Private deploys
- Performance benchmarking and acceptable SLOs
- Procurement steps and timelines

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro from our side, I'm Maya Patel, AE on the Redwood partnerships team. Diego's on the call to talk tech and benchmarks.
[00:12] Diego: Hey hi, Diego Ramos, I'm the systems engineer, I do the performance + infra stuff.
[00:18] Nora: Nora Lin here, Head of Platform at Firetrail. We run most workloads in GCP and a mix of colo for latency sensitive apps.
[00:25] Evan: Evan Cho, CTO. Nice to meet you all.
[00:29] Priya: Priya Nair, infra lead. I'll be the primary technical counterpart for any peering or private deployments.
[00:37] Samir: Samir Rao from procurement, just listening in.
[00:40] Maya: Great, thanks. Broad agenda — understand your stack, constraints, interest in Dedicated vs hosted and Private, and figure out next steps. Sound good?
[00:49] Nora: Yes that's perfect. I'll start with context — we have a product team building a realtime conversational assistant for EU customers, low-latency is important. We currently use GCP instances with some TPU/GPU for training but inference is mostly on a managed endpoint that's getting expensive.
[01:10] Evan: We're exploring options to reduce per-token cost while keeping median latencies under 120ms for short prompts and tail under 300ms. Also data residency rules mean EU data must not leave region.
[01:26] Maya: Understood. Quick clarification on workload shape — are these mostly short prompts, or longer context windows?
[01:33] Priya: Mostly short, under 256 tokens, but we have occasional longer context flows up to 2k tokens for logs summarization. Peak concurrency is around 400 qps during spikes, baseline 70-90 qps.
[01:47] Diego: Ok that's helpful. On Redwood we usually map that to model choice plus batching profile. For 256-token median, continuous batching plus prefix cache can drive cost down. We have Dedicated pools that give predictable throughput, and Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem cases.
[02:05] Evan: Can you describe the difference between Dedicated and Private in terms of network? We want to avoid putting customer data through public internet for EU customers.
[02:15] Maya: Sure. Dedicated is reserved capacity hosted in our cloud region — it's logically isolated, but still managed by Redwood. Private is where we set up a control plane in your VPC or an on-prem option so traffic stays in your network, and keys can be customer-managed KMS/HSM. There are tradeoffs on ops surface area.
[02:35] Priya: So Private supports VPC peering or AWS/GCP VPC peering? We need peering and mTLS for data plane.
[02:44] Diego: Yes we support VPC peering and private link models, mTLS is supported for in-transit encryption. Note sometimes the doc names get funny — folks call it Redwood Private, Redwood Dedicates — but the underlying capabilities are separate.
[02:57] Nora: On compliance — we require SOC2 type II and ISO-27001 artifacts plus audit logs, and SIEM integration. Do you have customer-managed log shipping or do you retain logs?
[03:09] Maya: We have a compliance pack, SOC2 and ISO certs, and we can do log forwarding to your SIEM or provide audit log export. For Private you can keep logs in your environment. I'll send the pack after the call.
[03:20] Samir: From procurement timeline — if we do a pilot how long does legal typically take? We have a standard vendor security review process.
[03:28] Maya: Usually security review + vendor terms can be 2–4 weeks for pilot. We also offer an initial non-prod pilot agreement that's faster.
[03:36] Evan: Cost question — what are the unit economics for Dedicated vs hosted API? We're trying to compare per-token cost and commitment.
[03:44] Diego: Hosted is pay-as-you-go per token, which is easiest. Dedicated is a reserved capacity model with monthly commit that lowers the per-token unit cost but requires capacity planning. We can provide example math for your workload.
[03:59] Priya: Do you have quantized model variants? We currently use an open model family and could consider 8-bit quantized variants to save cost.
[04:08] Diego: Yes — we support quantized runtimes and suggest profiles per workload. The runtime handles kernel selection and continuous batching; for some models going from fp16 to 8-bit can be 30-40% cost reduction with small latency impact. We'll suggest model + quant profile in the benchmark.
[04:23] Nora: Important: EU data residency — if we use Hosted in US region that won't work. Do you have EU regions for Hosted and Dedicated?
[04:31] Maya: Yes, we have Hosted and Dedicated capacity in EU-west and a Private option you can put inside your VPC in eu-west1. I'll include regional options in the doc.
[04:41] Evan: For the benchmark run — we'll want to run our sample convo and also a few production-like SLO queries. We want to measure median, p95, p99 latency, and token cost.
[04:52] Diego: Sounds good. Suggested benchmark: 2-hour run, sample set of 10k typical requests and a spike test to 500 qps for a 5 minute window. We'll capture latency histograms and token counts.
[05:03] Priya: Network question — can the inference nodes be inside our VPC so we don't leave the network for inference?
[05:09] Diego: Yes, that's a Private deployment. There's also a hybrid option where we place inference in your VPC and control plane is still Redwood-managed; depends on your compliance needs.
[05:19] Nora: Are there automated fallbacks — for example if Dedicated is saturated do you fall back to a cheaper hosted option?
[05:25] Maya: Yep, we have smart routing policies — you can set fallbacks by policy to route to a compatible smaller model or a hosted tier. That way you get graceful degradation rather than an outage.
[05:36] Samir: From procurement perspective, what are SLAs for Dedicated?
[05:40] Maya: Dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime and latency targets better than hosted; specifics depend on committed tier. I'll include draft SLA language in the pricing doc.
[05:50] Evan: Security integration: we use an HSM for KMS and strict key rotation. Is customer-managed KMS supported?
[05:56] Diego: Yes for Private we support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations. For Hosted you can opt in but it's often a managed KMS.
[06:06] Priya: Any constraints on model size or GPU types for Private? We tend to use A100/NVIDIA T4 in colo and sometimes Ampere instances.
[06:15] Diego: We support a range of GPU types; the runtime selects kernels and memory layout. For very large models we have sharding options. We'll propose the best fit based on your model family and inference profile.
[06:27] Nora: Who should we expect to be on the bench-run?
[06:30] Maya: Diego and I will run the Redwood side; recommend Priya and one engineer from your infra team to be on. We'll need sample prompts and a test dataset.
[06:38] Evan: Timeline — we want a pilot in the next 2–3 weeks if possible. Is that feasible?
[06:43] Maya: Yes, with security docs and an ETA for the benchmark we can kick off a pilot within 2 weeks.
[06:49] Priya: Network scheduling — I'll need an intro to your infra team to organize peering windows.
[06:53] Maya: I'll send an intro email right after this call.
[06:57] Nora: Any integration with our existing auth/SSO? We use SAML SSO and Okta.
[07:02] Diego: We support SSO/SAML and RBAC integrations. For Private we can sync to your IdP directly.
[07:08] Samir: Quick legal thing — do you have a standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA) for EU data?
[07:13] Maya: Yes we'll include a DPA template.
[07:16] Evan: One more — can you do request-level cost attribution per token set for our product teams? We need cost per feature.
[07:24] Diego: The Console gives token-level breakdown and per-route dashboards so you can attribute cost. We'll show an example in the follow-up.
[07:33] Nora: Okay let's recap next steps.
[07:36] Maya: Recap — I'll send security & compliance pack, DPA, and draft pricing for Dedicated vs hosted. Diego will scope the benchmark and propose timelines. Priya will coordinate peering and give us access for the perf runs. Evan will share expected throughput numbers and sample payloads. Samir you and procurement will queue the pilot agreement review.
[07:58] Evan: Sounds good. We're targeting a pilot decision by 2026-05-21.
[08:04] Maya: Great. We'll aim to have the benchmark booked and pricing sent by 2026-05-13 and get the security docs by 2026-05-12.
[08:12] Priya: I'll prepare network details and share them with Diego.
[08:16] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and I'll attach the compliance pack.
[08:21] Nora: Thanks, bye.

(end of transcript)
